segments.text: Hi there, this is lecture 4 in the Introduction to Photonics video series.
segments.zh: 大家好，这是光子学入门系列视频的第 4 讲。

segments.text: The title of this lecture is More on Properties of Light.
segments.zh: 本讲的题目是“光的性质续论”。

segments.text: In the previous three lectures, we laid foundations of photonics.
segments.zh: 在前三讲中，我们奠定了光子学的基础。

segments.text: We established the terminology that describes the light.
segments.zh: 我们建立了描述光的术语。

segments.text: We talked about different properties of light.
segments.zh: 我们讲了光的各种性质。

segments.text: We established the dual nature of light.
segments.zh: 我们确立了光的二象性。

segments.text: We talked about absorption and emission in the previous lecture.
segments.zh: 在上一讲中，我们讲了吸收和发射。

segments.text: This lecture number 4 takes us one step further.
segments.zh: 第 4 讲带我们再前进一步。

segments.text: We are going to expand on the topics related to the properties of light.
segments.zh: 我们将展开讲与光的性质有关的话题。

segments.text: We are going to expand on the stuff that we talked about in the previous three lectures.
segments.zh: 我们将展开讲前三讲中讲过的内容。

segments.text: Specifically, in this lecture, we are going to cover topics that are going to help us better understand
segments.zh: 具体来说，在本讲中，我们将讲一些话题，帮助我们更好地理解

segments.text: the nature of optical materials and their transmission and reflection characteristics as a function of the wavelength.
segments.zh: 光学材料的本质，以及它们的透射和反射特性随波长的变化。

segments.text: We are also going to talk about the selection of optical materials for specific use in the visible ultraviolet or infrared region.
segments.zh: 我们还将讲如何选择光学材料，用于可见光、紫外或红外区域的特定用途。

segments.text: Finally, we are going to explain how a single and multiple anti-reflection coatings and filters are made and used.
segments.zh: 最后，我们将解释单层和多层增透膜以及滤光片是如何制作和使用的。

segments.text: With this lecture, we are slowly moving in the direction of an optical lab.
segments.zh: 通过本讲，我们正慢慢地向光学实验室的方向迈进。

segments.text: We are going to start talking about optical components and different amounts that are to be found in a standard optical lab.
segments.zh: 我们将开始讲标准光学实验室中可以见到的光学元件和各种镜架。

segments.text: We are going to try to make a transition from the basic theoretical foundations of photonics into more of a practical concept.
segments.zh: 我们将尝试从光子学的基础理论过渡到更偏实用的概念。

segments.text: The first concept that we are going to mention is the optical materials that are to be found in an optical lab.
segments.zh: 我们要提到的第一个概念是光学实验室中可以见到的光学材料。

segments.text: We are going to find a large variety of different optical materials and different optical components.
segments.zh: 我们会见到种类繁多的不同光学材料和不同光学元件。

segments.text: In general, we can classify them in so-called non-transparent and also so-called transparent types of optical materials.
segments.zh: 一般来说，我们可以把它们分为所谓的不透明光学材料和所谓的透明光学材料。

segments.text: We are going to define each of these throughout this lecture.
segments.zh: 我们将在本讲中分别给出它们的定义。

segments.text: The first that we are going to talk about is the transparent optical medium.
segments.zh: 我们首先要讲的是透明光学介质。

segments.text: Everyone knows what transparent means.
segments.zh: 大家都知道透明是什么意思。

segments.text: The most popular definition when we say transparent means something that we can see through.
segments.zh: 我们说“透明”时，最常见的定义是指我们能透过它看东西。

segments.text: But if you want to kind of be more specific and use the term from the field of photonics,
segments.zh: 但如果你想说得更具体一些，用光子学领域的术语来说，

segments.text: we are going to define transparent optical medium as a medium that has a low absorption, low reflection,
segments.zh: 我们把透明光学介质定义为这样一种介质：它的吸收低、反射低，

segments.text: distortion of light that's passing through it is reduced to a minimum.
segments.zh: 通过它的光的畸变被降到最低。

segments.text: It also would have a high damage threshold for laser radiation.
segments.zh: 它对激光辐射还具有很高的损伤阈值。

segments.text: And finally, it's going to have a minimal optical degradation to different environmental effects,
segments.zh: 最后，它在各种环境影响下的光学性能退化极小，

segments.text: such as temperature, water vapor, and other hostile environment conditions.
segments.zh: 比如温度、水蒸气以及其他恶劣的环境条件。

segments.text: On this slide, we are going to further expand on the topic of our index of refraction.
segments.zh: 在这张幻灯片上，我们将进一步展开讲折射率这个话题。

segments.text: In one of the previous lectures, we defined index of refraction.
segments.zh: 在前面的一讲中，我们定义了折射率。

segments.text: We said that index of refraction represents a unitless quantity that characterizes a specific medium.
segments.zh: 我们说过，折射率是一个表征某种特定介质的无量纲量。

segments.text: Every medium has a specific index of refraction that defines optical properties of that material.
segments.zh: 每种介质都有特定的折射率，它决定了该材料的光学性质。

segments.text: To be more specific, index of refraction represents the number that shows us how much is the speed of light
segments.zh: 更具体地说，折射率是一个数，它告诉我们光速

segments.text: reduced in that specific medium relative to the speed of light in air or vacuum.
segments.zh: 在该特定介质中相对于空气或真空中的光速降低了多少。

segments.text: So once more, index of refraction or refractive index is defined as the ratio of the speed of light
segments.zh: 所以再说一遍，折射率被定义为光在

segments.text: in a vacuum to the speed of light in a particular medium.
segments.zh: 真空中的速度与光在某一特定介质中的速度之比。

segments.text: We are talking about a unitless quantity that's always greater than 1.
segments.zh: 我们说的是一个总是大于 1 的无量纲量。

segments.text: If index of refraction is equal to 1, it means that we are talking about the vacuum,
segments.zh: 如果折射率等于 1，就意味着我们说的是真空，

segments.text: we are talking about the medium that has a speed of light equal to the 3 times 10 to the 8 meters per second.
segments.zh: 我们说的是光速等于每秒 3 乘 10 的 8 次方米的介质。

segments.text: It's also important to understand that the index of refraction is also going to be a function of the wavelength.
segments.zh: 还要理解的重要一点是，折射率也是波长的函数。

segments.text: That's something new that we haven't mentioned before, and we are introducing on this specific slide.
segments.zh: 这是我们以前没有提到过的新内容，我们在这张幻灯片上介绍它。

segments.text: So if you're looking at a plot on our right-hand side, we see here two plots, three plots, three curves for three different types of material.
segments.zh: 所以如果你看右边的图，我们这里看到两条、三条曲线，对应三种不同的材料。

segments.text: On the top we have a crown glass, and then we have acrylic, and finally on the bottom we have a fused quartz.
segments.zh: 最上面是冕牌玻璃，然后是亚克力，最下面是熔融石英。

segments.text: On a horizontal x-axis are different wavelengths that are covering a visible spectrum ranging from 400 nanometers all the way to 700 nanometers,
segments.zh: 水平的 x 轴上是覆盖可见光谱的不同波长，从 400 纳米一直到 700 纳米，

segments.text: and then on the vertical axis we have the index of refraction.
segments.zh: 然后在纵轴上是折射率。

segments.text: You can see that these three curves are not flat. In other words, the index of refraction is changing with the wavelength.
segments.zh: 你可以看到这三条曲线并不平坦。换句话说，折射率随波长而变化。

segments.text: So for example, if you're looking at acrylic, which is a very popular type of medium used in many optical components in a photonics lab,
segments.zh: 所以例如，如果你看亚克力，它是一种非常常用的介质，用于光子学实验室的许多光学元件，

segments.text: we see that at the wavelength of red, the wavelength of violet, which is 400 nanometers, the index of refraction of acrylic is about 1.51.
segments.zh: 我们看到在红光的波长，在紫光的波长，也就是 400 纳米处，亚克力的折射率约为 1.51。

segments.text: And if you are going all the way to the right side, if you come closer to the 700 nanometers, which is the wavelength of red,
segments.zh: 如果你一直往右边走，接近 700 纳米，也就是红光的波长，

segments.text: we see that index of refraction of acrylic dropped from 1.51 all the way down to below 1.49.
segments.zh: 我们看到亚克力的折射率从 1.51 一直降到 1.49 以下。

segments.text: So these differences are relatively small, so we're talking here about the range of change from 1.51 to 1.49 in the case of acrylic,
segments.zh: 所以这些差异相对较小，对于亚克力，我们这里说的是从 1.51 到 1.49 的变化范围，

segments.text: but they are enough to produce a certain effect that we can very easily observe.
segments.zh: 但它们足以产生一种我们很容易观察到的效应。

segments.text: For example, if we have a prism that's made out of acrylic, if you're shooting the different colors of light,
segments.zh: 例如，如果我们有一个用亚克力做的棱镜，如果你射入不同颜色的光，

segments.text: those different colors will be refracted at different angles due to the fact that index of refraction is different for those different colors.
segments.zh: 这些不同的颜色会以不同的角度折射，因为不同颜色对应的折射率不同。

segments.text: In other words, if we are shooting white light through the prism made out of acrylic, what you'll see on the other side is that that white is going to be broken down into all the colors that it's made out of.
segments.zh: 换句话说，如果我们让白光通过用亚克力做的棱镜，你会在另一侧看到白光被分解成组成它的所有颜色。

segments.text: And that's exactly practical application of the concept that we're introducing on this specific slide.
segments.zh: 而这正是我们在这张幻灯片上介绍的概念的实际应用。

segments.text: So once more, index of refraction is a unit list quantity that describes the ratio of the speed of light in the vacuum to the speed of light in a specific medium.
segments.zh: 所以再说一遍，折射率是一个无量纲量，它描述的是光在真空中的速度与光在某一特定介质中的速度之比。

segments.text: And this unit list quantity is a function of the wavelength. In other words, it's changing with the wavelength. What we see on the right hand side is an example with three curves representing three different types of optical materials that are very popular materials used in photonics.
segments.zh: 而这个无量纲量是波长的函数。换句话说，它随波长而变化。我们在右边看到的是一个例子，有三条曲线，代表光子学中非常常用的三种不同光学材料。

segments.text: The next topic that we are going to expand in this lecture is a concept of absorption and transmission of light.
segments.zh: 本讲要展开的下一个话题是光的吸收和透射的概念。

segments.text: In the previous lecture, number three, we talked about particle properties of light.
segments.zh: 在上一讲，即第三讲中，我们讲了光的粒子性。

segments.text: And we translated those properties into specific phenomena that relate to the light, specifically interaction of light and the medium.
segments.zh: 我们把这些性质转化为与光有关的具体现象，特别是光与介质的相互作用。

segments.text: And we said that if light passes through a medium, an absorption phenomenon is taking place where the power of the light beam is being reduced as the light is propagating through that medium.
segments.zh: 我们说过，如果光通过某种介质，就会发生吸收现象，光束在该介质中传播时，其功率会降低。

segments.text: And why is that happening has been explained in the previous lecture. We talked about atomic model of a material.
segments.zh: 为什么会这样，在上一讲中已经解释过了。我们讲了材料的原子模型。

segments.text: We talked about different energy levels of different electrons, how they're moving from our lower to higher energy levels as they're absorbing the light, etc.
segments.zh: 我们讲了不同电子的不同能级，讲了它们在吸收光时如何从较低能级移到较高能级，等等。

segments.text: So on this slide, we are going to quantify that whole concept.
segments.zh: 所以在这张幻灯片上，我们要把整个概念定量化。

segments.text: So what you see on the right hand side is a plot of an optical window of a thickness x. So this optical window is made out of certain material.
segments.zh: 你在右边看到的是一块厚度为 x 的光学窗口的示意图。这块光学窗口由某种材料制成。

segments.text: And the property of material is specified through this so-called absorbing material coefficient alpha.
segments.zh: 而材料的性质通过这个所谓的材料吸收系数 α 来表示。

segments.text: So this number alpha is changing with different media.
segments.zh: 所以这个数 α 随介质不同而变化。

segments.text: From the left hand side, we have an incident light that carries a certain power.
segments.zh: 从左边来的是携带一定功率的入射光。

segments.text: And here we are also going to introduce the concept of so-called irradiance. Irradiance represents the power over the area.
segments.zh: 这里我们还要引入所谓辐照度的概念。辐照度表示单位面积上的功率。

segments.text: So if you are, for example, looking at two different laser beams, and let's say both of those laser beams are carrying power of 10 watts.
segments.zh: 所以例如，如果你看两束不同的激光束，假设这两束激光的功率都是 10 瓦。

segments.text: However, one of the laser beams is very wide, while the other one is very thin.
segments.zh: 但是，其中一束激光很宽，而另一束很细。

segments.text: The effect that a thin laser beam is going to make on the material is going to be much larger than the effect that a wider beam is going to make, although both of them are carrying the same power of 10 watts.
segments.zh: 细激光束对材料产生的效应会比宽光束产生的效应大得多，尽管两者携带的功率都是 10 瓦。

segments.text: So in order to capture that type of effect, we have to look at a different quantity that's going to take into account both the power on the one side and then also the area or the thickness or if you wish, the width of the beam of that light.
segments.zh: 所以为了描述这类效应，我们必须看另一个量，它一方面考虑功率，另一方面还考虑光束的面积，或者说粗细，或者如果你愿意，也可以说是光束的宽度。

segments.text: And that quantity is so-called irradiance. So we define irradiance as a power of a specific area.
segments.zh: 这个量就是所谓的辐照度。所以我们把辐照度定义为单位面积上的功率。

segments.text: So this incident light that you're seeing here coming from the left side and entering the optical window is going to have a specific irradiance, E0, and it also is specified by the wavelength lambda.
segments.zh: 所以你在这里看到的这束从左边来、进入光学窗口的入射光，会有一个特定的辐照度 E0，它还由波长 λ 来表征。

segments.text: What we also see is that same beam of light exits the optical window. We see that irradiance changed. It's not anymore E0.
segments.zh: 我们还看到，同一束光从光学窗口射出。我们看到辐照度改变了，不再是 E0。

segments.text: Now it is equal to capital E. In other words, the irradiance has changed because a certain amount of power has been absorbed in this optical medium.
segments.zh: 现在它等于大写 E。换句话说，辐照度改变了，因为有一定的功率在这种光学介质中被吸收了。

segments.text: The question is how we can quantify, how we can calculate what is the power, what is the irradiance on the right side compared to the irradiance on the left side.
segments.zh: 问题是我们如何定量描述、如何计算右边的功率、右边的辐照度与左边的辐照度相比是多少。

segments.text: What is the comparison between the output power that exits the optical window and the input power that enters this optical window?
segments.zh: 从光学窗口射出的输出功率与进入这块光学窗口的输入功率相比如何？

segments.text: It turns out that there is a specific formula, there is a specific law that's shown here in a box on the left-hand side where the output irradiance E is a function of the input irradiance E0
segments.zh: 结果表明，有一个专门的公式，有一条专门的定律，显示在左边的方框中，其中输出辐照度 E 是输入辐照度 E0 的函数，

segments.text: and then also a function of the type of material that's captured to the coefficient alpha and then also is a function of the thickness of the window that's captured to the parameter x.
segments.zh: 也是材料类型的函数，材料类型由系数 α 体现，同时还是窗口厚度的函数，窗口厚度由参数 x 体现。

segments.text: So once more E0, capital E0 represents the incident irradiance, incident power per unit area.
segments.zh: 所以再说一遍，E0，大写 E0，表示入射辐照度，即单位面积上的入射功率。

segments.text: Capital E is going to capture the transmitted irradiance or the output irradiance.
segments.zh: 大写 E 表示透射辐照度，或者说输出辐照度。

segments.text: Alpha is an absorption coefficient in the units of reciprocal length that captures the properties of the material that optical window is made out of and finally x represents the thickness of the optical window.
segments.zh: α 是吸收系数，单位是长度的倒数，它体现了光学窗口所用材料的性质，最后 x 表示光学窗口的厚度。

segments.text: And we see that through the formula, through the law that's being shown here, the output irradiance is going to be the function of the input irradiance,
segments.zh: 我们看到，通过这个公式，通过这里所示的这条定律，输出辐照度是输入辐照度、

segments.text: type of material that optical window is made out of and finally thickness of that window.
segments.zh: 光学窗口所用材料的类型以及窗口厚度的函数。

segments.text: We can also define so-called transmittance. The transmittance is basically a representation of how much percentage wise of the input power has been transmitted over to the other side of this optical window.
segments.zh: 我们还可以定义所谓的透射率。透射率基本上表示输入功率中有百分之多少透射到了这块光学窗口的另一侧。

segments.text: So if we take a ratio of the output irradiance E and the input irradiance E0 and multiply by 100, we are going to get so-called transmittance.
segments.zh: 所以如果我们取输出辐照度 E 与输入辐照度 E0 之比，再乘以 100，就得到所谓的透射率。

segments.text: That's going to be the percentage quantity.
segments.zh: 它是一个百分比量。

segments.text: So it's very easy if we apply the formula from the previous slide to see that this transmittance, the quantity transmittance, is going to be determined by the properties of this optical window and also the thickness of the window.
segments.zh: 所以如果我们应用上一张幻灯片中的公式，很容易看出，这个透射率，透射率这个量，是由这块光学窗口的性质以及窗口的厚度决定的。

segments.text: So we can also observe that the absorption coefficient alpha depends on the nature of the material and the wavelength of the light.
segments.zh: 所以我们还可以观察到，吸收系数 α 取决于材料的性质和光的波长。

segments.text: It's also important to mention that most of the optical glass materials, transparent materials that are being used in photonics labs, would transmit nearly 100% of the visible light,
segments.zh: 还要提到的重要一点是，光子学实验室中使用的大多数光学玻璃材料、透明材料，几乎能透过 100% 的可见光，

segments.text: meaning the entire range from the near ultraviolet all the way to the near infrared.
segments.zh: 也就是从近紫外一直到近红外的整个范围。

segments.text: Now that we established the parameter transmittance, let's shift out our focus to the transmission properties of different optical materials used in the field of photonics.
segments.zh: 既然我们确定了透射率这个参数，我们就把注意力转到光子学领域中使用的不同光学材料的透射特性上。

segments.text: So let's look at a fused silica and fused quartz first. These two materials are very popular and have been used for many types of optical components that are used in the photonics lab.
segments.zh: 所以我们先来看熔融石英玻璃和熔融石英。这两种材料非常常用，已被用于光子学实验室中使用的许多类型的光学元件。

segments.text: And it turns out that these two materials are used in the ultraviolet region from 0.2 to 0.4 micrometers.
segments.zh: 结果表明，这两种材料用于 0.2 到 0.4 微米的紫外区域。

segments.text: We also have a whole bunch of different glasses that have reduced transmission beyond 3.4 microns in the infrared region, etc.
segments.zh: 我们还有一大堆不同的玻璃，它们在红外区域超过 3.4 微米后透射率降低，等等。

segments.text: So we can identify a whole bunch of different types of materials. We mentioned here fused silica and fused quartz.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以列出一大堆不同类型的材料。我们这里提到了熔融石英玻璃和熔融石英。

segments.text: We also have a Pyrex, we have a Zerodur, etc. Now, it's also important to spend a few minutes explaining what you're seeing here on this plot on the left-hand side.
segments.zh: 我们还有 Pyrex，有 Zerodur，等等。现在，花几分钟解释一下你在左边这张图上看到的内容也很重要。

segments.text: What you see here are the transmission properties of a few different types of materials.
segments.zh: 你在这里看到的是几种不同材料的透射特性。

segments.text: On the bottom, on the horizontal axis, you have a wavelength, and then on the vertical axis, you have a transmittance in terms of percentage.
segments.zh: 在底部的水平轴上是波长，然后在纵轴上是以百分比表示的透射率。

segments.text: So for example, let's focus on the curve D that represents the curve for the material called Zerodur.
segments.zh: 所以例如，我们来重点看曲线 D，它代表一种叫 Zerodur 的材料的曲线。

segments.text: You can see that Zerodur has a relatively high transmittance in the range of, let's say, 0.7 microns all the way to, let's say, 3 microns.
segments.zh: 你可以看到，Zerodur 在大约 0.7 微米一直到大约 3 微米的范围内透射率相对较高。

segments.text: So 0.7 microns is about 700 nanometers and above. So 700 nanometers and above, we are talking about infrared region.
segments.zh: 0.7 微米大约是 700 纳米及以上。所以 700 纳米及以上，我们说的是红外区域。

segments.text: As we are moving to the wavelengths below the infrared, if you're entering the visible spectrum, so from 0.7 microns up to 0.7 microns or 400 nanometers to 700 nanometers that represents the visible spectrum,
segments.zh: 当我们移到红外以下的波长，如果进入可见光谱，也就是从 0.7 微米到 0.7 微米，或者说 400 纳米到 700 纳米，这代表可见光谱，

segments.text: you see that the transmittance of Zerodur significantly degrades to the point where at the wavelength of 400 nanometers that represents the violet color, we have the transmittance of about 30%.
segments.zh: 你会看到 Zerodur 的透射率明显下降，以至于在代表紫色的 400 纳米波长处，透射率约为 30%。

segments.text: So what this shows us is that this type of material, Zerodur, has a very, very different transmission properties at different wavelengths.
segments.zh: 所以这告诉我们，Zerodur 这种材料在不同波长上的透射特性非常非常不同。

segments.text: So if our goal is to create the optical component that is passing most of light in the infrared region while it is blocking a significant amount of light in the visible and ultraviolet region,
segments.zh: 所以如果我们的目标是制作这样一种光学元件，它让红外区域的大部分光通过，同时挡住可见光和紫外区域的大量光，

segments.text: then this material may be a good candidate because, as I said, in infrared region, the transmittance of this material is around 90%, in other words, almost all the light, 90% of the light that's in infrared region will be passing through Zerodur.
segments.zh: 那么这种材料可能是一个很好的候选，因为正如我所说，在红外区域，这种材料的透射率约为 90%，换句话说，几乎所有的光，红外区域 90% 的光都会透过 Zerodur。

segments.text: You can draw similar conclusions for other materials, for other three materials, meaning fused silica, fused quartz, and pyrex from the other three curves A, B, and C on this plot.
segments.zh: 对于其他材料，对于其他三种材料，也就是熔融石英玻璃、熔融石英和 Pyrex，你可以根据这张图上的另外三条曲线 A、B 和 C 得出类似的结论。

segments.text: So what you are seeing on this slide, this plot, is actually very important. So if you are working as a photonics technician in a photonics lab and you are operating a specific type of a laser or different type of optical system and you need to have a good transmission properties, transmission characteristics in infrared region,
segments.zh: 所以你在这张幻灯片上、这张图上看到的内容实际上非常重要。所以如果你在光子学实验室当光子学技术员，你在操作某种激光器或其他类型的光学系统，你需要在红外区域有良好的透射性能、透射特性，

segments.text: then you would be analyzing, if you are selecting a specific optical component made out of a specific material, you would want to look at the transmission characteristic of that medium, so you would be analyzing the curves similar to those that you are seeing here on this slide.
segments.zh: 那么你就要分析，如果你要选择用某种材料制成的某个光学元件，你就要看那种介质的透射特性，所以你会分析类似于你在这张幻灯片上看到的这些曲线。

segments.text: This slide further elaborates the properties of different optical materials that are used in the field of photonics. So here, a table is shown.
segments.zh: 这张幻灯片进一步阐述光子学领域中使用的不同光学材料的性质。这里显示了一张表格。

segments.text: On the left side, you have a column that specifies different types of materials, and then, you know, there's a few other columns, columns that show the wavelength range, refractive index, and finally, certain other properties of this media.
segments.zh: 左边有一列列出了不同类型的材料，然后还有另外几列，显示波长范围、折射率，最后是这些介质的一些其他性质。

segments.text: So these types of tables start being very handy if you are performing certain types of experiments that involve these materials in a photonic lab.
segments.zh: 所以如果你在光子学实验室中进行涉及这些材料的某些类型的实验，这类表格就会变得非常有用。

segments.text: Starting with this slide, we are shifting our focus from absorption and transmission to the concept of surface reflection.
segments.zh: 从这张幻灯片开始，我们把注意力从吸收和透射转到表面反射的概念上。

segments.text: So we are still looking at the boundary between the two media, as shown in the picture on the left side.
segments.zh: 所以我们仍然看两种介质之间的边界，如左边的图所示。

segments.text: You can see that here we are dealing with the air on the left-hand side, and we are dealing with the glass on the right-hand side.
segments.zh: 你可以看到，这里左边是空气，右边是玻璃。

segments.text: Each of these two media are characterized by the index of refraction. In the case of air, we are dealing with the index of refraction equal to one.
segments.zh: 这两种介质各自用折射率来表征。对于空气，折射率等于 1。

segments.text: And then, in the case of a glass, we are dealing with a type of glass that has index of refraction equal to 1.5.
segments.zh: 然后对于玻璃，我们这里是一种折射率等于 1.5 的玻璃。

segments.text: So what are we interested in this case here is what is happening when the light hits the boundary between the air and the glass.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们感兴趣的是光照射到空气和玻璃之间的边界时会发生什么。

segments.text: We know that, according to the wave properties, there is going to be a certain reflection of light from this boundary.
segments.zh: 我们知道，根据波动性质，光会在这个边界上发生一定的反射。

segments.text: We can use the law of reflection to determine the direction of the reflected beam.
segments.zh: 我们可以用反射定律来确定反射光束的方向。

segments.text: But what we are interested on this slide to determine is what is the power, what is the irradiance that is in that reflected beam.
segments.zh: 但我们在这张幻灯片上想确定的是，反射光束中的功率是多少，辐照度是多少。

segments.text: So that's what is basically being represented on this picture that's shown on the left-hand side.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上就是左边这张图所表示的内容。

segments.text: It turns out that reflection, or so-called reflectance, which is going to basically be equal to the percentage of the input power that's being reflected,
segments.zh: 结果表明，反射，或者说所谓的反射率，它基本上等于输入功率中被反射的百分比，

segments.text: is a function of the two indices of refraction of the two media.
segments.zh: 是两种介质的两个折射率的函数。

segments.text: So the formula, the equation that you are seeing on the right-hand side, defines so-called reflectance.
segments.zh: 所以你在右边看到的公式、方程，定义了所谓的反射率。

segments.text: So once more, reflectance is equal to the ratio of the reflected irradiance to the input irradiance or incident irradiance.
segments.zh: 所以再说一遍，反射率等于反射辐照度与输入辐照度或入射辐照度之比。

segments.text: And it's a function of the two numbers, N1 and N2, according to the equation that you are seeing on the right-hand side.
segments.zh: 根据你在右边看到的方程，它是 N1 和 N2 这两个数的函数。

segments.text: So if we plug in the values for the index of refraction, N1 equal to 1, and index of refraction equal to 1.5 for the second medium,
segments.zh: 所以如果我们代入折射率的值，N1 等于 1，第二种介质的折射率等于 1.5，

segments.text: and do calculation, we are going to come up with the value of reflectance being equal to 4%.
segments.zh: 然后进行计算，就会得到反射率等于 4%。

segments.text: This number 4% means that out of the total input irradiance that is in an incident ray, 4% is going to get reflected,
segments.zh: 4% 这个数意味着，在入射光线的全部输入辐照度中，有 4% 会被反射，

segments.text: while the rest of 96% is going to get transmitted into the glass.
segments.zh: 而其余 96% 会透射进入玻璃。

segments.text: And then as this transmitted ray that's equal to 96% of the incident irradiance is going to be absorbed slowly as the light beam is moving through the glass.
segments.zh: 然后，这条等于入射辐照度 96% 的透射光线，在光束穿过玻璃的过程中会被慢慢吸收。

segments.text: So using the formula on the right-hand side, we have determined the reflectance at the boundary between the air and the glass
segments.zh: 所以利用右边的公式，我们确定了空气和玻璃之间边界上的反射率，

segments.text: as a function of the two indices of refraction of the first medium, in our case air, and the second medium in our case glass.
segments.zh: 它是第一种介质（在我们这里是空气）和第二种介质（在我们这里是玻璃）这两个折射率的函数。

segments.text: The next case that we are going to analyze is a case of an optical window.
segments.zh: 我们要分析的下一种情况是光学窗口的情况。

segments.text: So in this case, we not only have the first boundary between the air and the glass, but also the second boundary from the glass back into the air.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们不仅有从空气到玻璃的第一个边界，还有从玻璃回到空气的第二个边界。

segments.text: So what of interest here is, again, how much light is going to get reflected from such an optical window.
segments.zh: 所以这里我们感兴趣的仍然是，从这样一块光学窗口会反射多少光。

segments.text: What's important to notice here is that we don't have just one single reflection, as in the case of the single boundary between the air and the glass,
segments.zh: 这里需要注意的重要一点是，我们不是只有一次反射，不像空气和玻璃之间只有一个边界的情况，

segments.text: but we have all these multiple reflections. How are these multiple reflections established?
segments.zh: 而是有所有这些多次反射。这些多次反射是怎么形成的呢？

segments.text: So let's look at the incident light beam.
segments.zh: 我们来看入射光束。

segments.text: So this incident light beam is going to hit the first boundary, and there's going to be a first single reflection that we calculated in the previous case to be equal to 4% in the case of a glass being equal to 1.5.
segments.zh: 这束入射光束会照射到第一个边界上，会有第一次反射，我们在前面的情况中算出，当玻璃为 1.5 时，它等于 4%。

segments.text: Now, the rest of the irradiance is going to get transmitted into the window, is going to continue propagating towards the right side.
segments.zh: 现在，其余的辐照度会透射进入窗口，继续向右传播。

segments.text: And then when that light beam reaches the second boundary between the glass and the air, a certain amount of that power is going to get reflected back into the window while the rest is going to be transmitted into the air.
segments.zh: 然后当这束光到达玻璃和空气之间的第二个边界时，一部分功率会被反射回窗口内，而其余部分会透射进入空气。

segments.text: So the reflected amount of light that's from the second boundary is going to propagate back towards the first boundary.
segments.zh: 所以从第二个边界反射的那部分光会向回传播到第一个边界。

segments.text: And then the first boundary, a certain amount is going to get reflected back into the window, but also a certain amount is going to get transmitted into the air, and it's going to show up as the second reflection.
segments.zh: 然后在第一个边界上，一部分会被反射回窗口内，但也有一部分会透射进入空气，作为第二次反射出现。

segments.text: And then we have all this bouncing back and forth of the light. So the light is going to be bouncing back and forth in the window, a certain amount of that light is going to get transmitted, a certain amount of that light is going to get reflected.
segments.zh: 然后光就这样来回反弹。所以光会在窗口中来回反弹，其中一部分光会透射出去，一部分光会被反射。

segments.text: And we're going to have all these multiple reflections that are going to be showing up in the air on the left hand side.
segments.zh: 于是我们会有所有这些多次反射，出现在左边的空气中。

segments.text: So what you can see here in this case, due to these multiple reflections, the amount of light that's going to get cumulatively reflected is going to be much, it's going to be more, it's going to be larger than the amount of light or irradiance
segments.zh: 所以你在这里可以看到，在这种情况下，由于这些多次反射，累计反射的光量会大得多，会更多，会大于

segments.text: in the case of the single reflection as we had in the previous case. So the formula that we established on the previous slide, where the reflectance has been defined as a function of the indices of refraction and one and then two,
segments.zh: 上一种情况中单次反射的光量或辐照度。所以我们在上一张幻灯片中建立的公式，其中反射率被定义为折射率 n1 和 n2 的函数，

segments.text: that formula has to be scratched in our case, and we have to establish a different type of a formula that's going to take into account all these multiple infractions that are showing up in the case of an optical window with the two boundaries,
segments.zh: 这个公式在我们这里就不适用了，我们必须建立另一种公式，把具有两个边界的光学窗口中出现的所有这些多次反射都考虑进去，

segments.text: one on the left side and one on the right side. So after a certain derivations, we can come up with a new set of formulas that are shown here on this slide.
segments.zh: 左边一个边界，右边一个边界。所以经过一些推导，我们可以得到这张幻灯片上所示的一组新公式。

segments.text: So the first thing that you're going to calculate is the quantity n sub r that's going to be equal to the ratio of the index of refraction of the window and the medium.
segments.zh: 所以你首先要计算的是 n 下标 r 这个量，它等于窗口折射率与介质折射率之比。

segments.text: So in our case, we have index of refraction of the window, which is going to be equal to 1.6, and then index of refraction of the medium is the index of refraction of the medium that surrounds this window in our case is going to be air.
segments.zh: 所以在我们这里，窗口的折射率等于 1.6，而介质的折射率就是这块窗口周围介质的折射率，在我们这里就是空气。

segments.text: So you're going to take again 1.6 over 1, come up with a value for the n subscript r, and then you're going to substitute the value of this n subscript r factor into the formula on the left hand side and calculate the total reflectance.
segments.zh: 所以你还是取 1.6 除以 1，得到 n 下标 r 的值，然后把这个 n 下标 r 因子的值代入左边的公式，计算总反射率。

segments.text: If you do that, you're going to see that this total reflectance is going to be more than 4% as in the case of a single boundary where the window is of infinite thickness.
segments.zh: 如果你这样做，你会看到这个总反射率会大于 4%，后者是窗口无限厚、只有单个边界时的情况。

segments.text: So the difference, again, between the two formulas, two equations or two cases, is the fact that in the case of the window of finite thickness, we have multiple reflections that have to be taken into account in the total cumulative reflectance that we want to determine in this specific example.
segments.zh: 所以这两个公式、两个方程或者说两种情况之间的区别，同样在于，对于有限厚度的窗口，我们有多次反射，必须把它们计入这个具体例子中我们想确定的总累计反射率。

segments.text: And then there's also a few other slides here that I skipped, such as this one here that talks a little bit about absorption filters.

So this can serve as an introductory assignment or introductory exercise for the next lecture number five, where we are going to go and talk more about the different types of filters that you may come across
segments.zh: 你可以设定滤光片通带的范围或宽度。你可以改变颜色。所以这可以作为下一讲，即第五讲的入门作业或入门练习，在那一讲中我们将进一步讲你可能遇到的各种类型的滤光片，

segments.text: in a typical photonics lab. So with this one, I'm going to conclude the lecture number four. Please study this material in the next lecture. As I said, we're going to go into the filters and then move further into different practical aspects of a typical photonics lab.
segments.zh: 它们在典型的光子学实验室中都能见到。所以就这样，我来结束第四讲。请学习这些材料，在下一讲中，正如我所说，我们将讲滤光片，然后进一步讲典型光子学实验室的各种实际方面。

segments.text: With this, I wish you a pleasant rest of the day and see you next time.
segments.zh: 就这样，祝你今天余下的时间愉快，我们下次见。
